practices.practice: Pick the vector index algorithm appropriate to dataset scale and SLA: use IVF for small demos, HNSW for high-recall workloads on M30+, and DiskANN for production at large scale (DiskANN recommended for very large collections).

practices.practice: Set and tune algorithm-specific vector-index parameters (dimensions, m / maxDegree, efConstruction / lBuild, efSearch / lSearch, numLists for IVF) to balance recall, build time, memory usage and search latency.
practices.prior_belief: For vector fields, create a vector index configured with the correct dimensionality and similarity metric (cosine) and tune the ANN algorithm parameters (e.g., algorithm=hnsw, M and efConstruction / efSearch or equivalent) appropriate to the index implementation to balance recall and query cost.

practices.practice: Store vectors as numeric arrays (number[]) and index them only via the platform's vector-index mechanisms; vector paths accept one vector per path and only one vector index per path.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the vector field excluded from default (B-tree) indexes and only index it via the platform's dedicated vector index mechanism; also exclude large text blobs from general indexing to reduce RU costs.

practices.practice: Use the $search aggregation stage with the cosmosSearch/cosmosSearchOptions operator as the first stage for vector (and hybrid) queries, target the index by name, and compose filtering via compound so the search index narrows candidates before other pipeline stages.
practices.prior_belief: Implement server-side or driver-side paging for any candidate filtering step (avoid reading entire collection into memory) and apply filtered vector search (candidate pre-filter by category/brand) before KNN to reduce compute and RU costs.

practices.practice: Project only the fields the UI needs (for example product_id, title, price, thumbnail) in queries and avoid returning the full embedding vector in API responses unless required to reduce RU and network costs.
practices.prior_belief: When returning the top-K substitutes, limit how much document data is read from disk: projection the response to only fields needed by the UI (product_id, title, price, thumbnail) and avoid returning the full embedding vector unless necessary.

practices.practice: For large-scale ingestion use SDK bulk execution where available (AllowBulkExecution) or parallel async/concurrent writes in Python; use batching and concurrency to maximize throughput and avoid one-document-at-a-time inserts.
practices.prior_belief: During bulk ingestion of 10,000 product transactions, use batching and the bulkWrite API (or driver bulk inserts) with sizes like 500–2000 documents per batch instead of inserting one document at a time, to reduce latency and RU consumption.

practices.practice: Do not assume driver-level options (like serverSelectionTimeoutMS or exact maxPoolSize values) are prescribed by Azure DocumentDB; consult language-specific quickstarts and tune driver timeouts/pools to your environment—Python quickstarts show examples with maxIdleTimeMS and retryWrites=false but do not prescribe exact pool sizes.

notes:
I inspected the sample app files (config, main, models, routes, ingest and quick verification scripts) and then searched Microsoft documentation for Azure DocumentDB (the product pages on docs.microsoft.com). The public docs provide detailed guidance for connection strings, authentication (including Microsoft Entra/managed identities), network controls (firewall/Private Link), single-client lifetime usage, vector-index algorithms (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) and index parameters (m, efConstruction, efSearch, lBuild, lSearch, numLists, dimensions), the requirement that vectors be numeric arrays (number[]), $search usage and $meta searchScore projection, bulk ingestion/batch and SDK bulk features, and monitoring/retry guidance for 429s and RU monitoring. Where a prior belief was a general app practice not found in Azure DocumentDB docs (K18) I marked it prior_knowledge_only. One prior belief (K19 recommending float32-only) is contradicted by public docs which explicitly describe half-precision and product quantization as supported options; I recorded the service guidance as the practice for that belief.

Prior beliefs the discovery step did not classify: K04. See 05a-prior-beliefs.json.
